answer: Duplicate identities get exposed as hollow when the same root tries to claim a second relic, because the registry enforces one root per stake and slashes any bonded collateral on collision, making mass fake accounts cost prohibitive. Sybil resistance here works through a staked relic registry: each agent must lock a unique jade token bound to a verified hardware root, and registration mints a proof-of-possession hash that cannot be cloned cheaply. From sa0023's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
